An employee lost his balance and fell while getting out of a dump truck. He suffered a broken hip.
An employee was installing a metal roof on the second story of a building. The employee fell from the roof to the ground, suffering a broken hip and a hand laceration.

An employee was performing a hot tap. The employee set a completion plug in preparation of removing the completion plug stopple tool. The tool was not completely set, and gas pressure and metal debris were released from the blow out. The employee sustained multiple contusions and abrasions to the chest, neck and face area, loss of eyes, and finger amputations.

An employee was helping to pour concrete and was using a concrete rake to spread the material in front of a vibratory concrete screed connected to a truck. The truck moved, causing the screed to knock the employee over and pass over him. He suffered a chest abrasion and crush injuries (without fractures) to the legs.

A dowel was being drilled into the side of a concrete paving foundation. The hammer drill bit would not stay centered on the foundation. An employee was stabilizing the hammer drill bit when it caught the employee's glove. The glove and the employee's left thumb were wrapped around the drill bit. The employee was hospitalized with a severed and dislocated thumb and they required surgery to reattach the thumb.

At 1:25 p.m. on March 13, 2025, a Michels Pacific Energy (MPE) crew was terminating new wires connecting a new three-phase sector and an existing pad-mounted switch elbow connected switch gear 20 feet away. The circuit being worked on was de-energized and isolated. All other circuits in the switch gear were insulated with insulating caps. After termination of the elbow, a strand of the new concentric neutral wire, used for bleeding capacitance, moved and made contact with the insulated bushing cover in the switch gear. The concentric neutral became energized from induced current at an unknown voltage. An employee working in the new sector was shocked on the right hand.

An employee was clearing a hopper with a hand shovel. He stepped off the ramp leading to the hopper and fell to the ground about 6 feet below, suffering a tear to the left lung, four broken ribs, and pelvic fractures.
An employee was installing rebar for a cinderblock wall that was being built. The top of the rebar made contact with a power line and the employee was shocked.

An employee was working from the top of a trailer, applying silicone to gutters on a gas station canopy. He stepped off the trailer and fell, suffering broken ribs as well as lacerations to the head and an elbow.

A crew was priming a cement pump. To help grout start moving through the pump, they ran a few gallons of water through it and started it in forward until the grout reached the end of the first 20-foot hose section. They then placed the pump in neutral, connected the next 20-foot hose with hose clamps, and began pumping again. As the grout traveled through the second hose, it clogged. The pump was put in neutral just as the hose kicked, and the motion traveled down the length of the hose. An employee was holding the end of the hose when it kicked up and struck him in the left side of the face, causing fractures.

An employee was soldering copper pipe extension to the cold-water main valve connection using a torch with a 13.5-pound propane tank. Lint from the nearby laundry chute caught on fire and smoke engulfed the bathroom area. The employee was hospitalized due to smoke inhalation.
On March 14, 2025, a painter was working on the fourth floor of a building. The employee fell through an elevator shaft and suffered a broken arm and leg.

An employee was working in a tight 15-inch space and using a 6-inch angle grinder to cut off an angle on an iron standoff boiler pulverizer. The grinder bound up in the angle, kicked back, lacerating the employee's left forearm.

On March 14, 2025, an employee was working from a roof overhang, installing siding. The employee fell to the ground about 40 feet below, suffering two fractures to the spine and open fractures to both feet. Fall protection was not in place at the time.

An employee was climbing an extended ladder to access the attic at the fourth floor level to inspect and blow debris off a flat roof. He turned sideways and grabbed a hand blower that was resting on an A-frame ladder next to him. He went to move up when the ladder slipped and he fell 8 to 9 feet straight down to the concrete ground. He landed on his feet and sustained a fractured L4 vertebra.
An employee was walking across a site to get rebar when he stepped on a wooden stake. The stake broke, causing the employee to sustain fractures to his left ankle/leg and lacerations.
An employee was entering a building through a doorway when wind caught the door and pinched their left little finger against a brick wall, resulting in an amputation halfway to the first knuckle.

An employee was standing on a 4-foot ladder. They went to push a piece of metal conduit up. A wire in the junction box came loose and electrified the conduit, causing the employee to sustain an electric shock.

On March 15, 2025, an employee was inspecting the roof of a one-story home. The employee was about to climb down the ladder from the roof when they slipped on felt paper and fell to the ground. The employee was hospitalized with six broken ribs, a broken collarbone, and a punctured lung.
An employee was installing insulation while on a ladder. He fell approximately 8 feet to the floor and fractured his right femur.

An employee was working from a 6-foot step ladder to look for a possible concrete wall opening to run a wire. The employee lifted up a ceiling tile and turned his torso to look at the area above the ceiling tiles. The ladder shifted and the employee fell approximately 4 feet to the concrete floor, striking their hip and lower back. The employee sustained a spinal fracture in their lower back.
On March 17, 2025, an employee was looking for an exhaust leak on a wheel loader when their left little finger contacted the fan, resulting in a fingertip amputation.

An employee was moving a 20-foot-long steel beam using an overhead crane. After lowering the beam onto dunnage wood, the employee unhooked it and began to move the crane. The crane's lifting attachment, which had not been fully removed, lifted the beam and caused it to roll toward a nearby pile of steel. The beam pushed the employee into the pile of steel and he suffered a broken leg.
An employee was using a hydraulic drive to extract a soil sample. The employee's index finger got caught in a pinch point of the bore mechanism, resulting in a partial amputation.

A subcontractor employee on a construction site was cleaning a unit. They were taking trash from the middle room when they fell through a door opening and landed approximately 25 feet below on a concrete pad. The employee was hospitalized with injuries to their shoulders and right side ribs.

An employee was climbing into a skid steer after picking up debris when his left foot got caught on the bucket release. He was removing himself from the bucket release when the skid steer ran over both of his feet, resulting in fractured feet and dislocated ankles.

On 3/17/2025, at 10:10 AM, two power poles were being framed at the same time on the back of a trailer. The injured employee reached to the other side of his pole to hold a nut for a bolt that was being pushed through. The employee on the other pole was drilling through his pole. The drill bit pushed through and contacted the injured employee's left little finger. The drill bit punctured the fingernail, causing a laceration and fracture.

An employee was guiding a riding trowel into a truck bed as it was being moved by a crane when his fingers became caught between the truck bed and the trowel. The employee sustained a partial amputation of his left index finger.
An employee was trimming tree branches at a client property. The employee was climbing the tree when they fell 10 feet to the ground, suffering fractured vertebrae.
An employee was walking when they tripped on a pallet jack and fell to the floor, resulting in a knee injury.
Two employees were removing a pressure safety valve when chlorine gas was released. The injured employee suffered upper respiratory irritation due to the chlorine gas.
An employee was using a circular saw while on a ladder. The blade of the saw contacted and amputated his right index finger.

An employee was working in bucket truck performing telecommunication maintenance. While the employee was tightening a lashing wire span, the strand slipped from the support clamp. The falling strand caused the lashing wire to sever the end of employee's left index fingertip, resulting in a partial amputation.

On March 18, 2025, an employee was working with a crew to remove a drill bit that was going to be replaced. The employee was using a breaking wrench to remove the drill bit when their hand got caught between the wrench and a hydraulic cylinder, resulting in a right thumb fracture that required hospitalization.
An employee was attaching a pintle hitch to a truck hitch in order to load a trailer. The employee's index finger was pinched between the hitches, resulting in a fingertip amputation.
An employee was lowering the excavator bucket. The employee placed his hand underneath to hook a chain and his right index finger and thumb got caught in the chain, resulting in partial amputations.
An employee was pulling a piece of decking backward when his leg hit a column base plate and he fell 15 feet from the fourth floor to the third-floor deck, resulting in a broken right femur.
An employee was rolling a pipe on a cart in order to paint the other side when the pipe slipped, pinching employee's finger against the cart and resulting in a fingertip amputation.

A crew was using a chain fall system to rig up a hard stop (metal structural support weighing 695 lbs.). The injured employee was guiding it into position. The hard stop shifted and their right hand was caught between the suspended hard stop and the adjacent structural wall, resulting in fractured ring and little fingers.
An employee was using a circular saw to cut a piece of 2 x 4 when the piece jumped forward and he sustained amputated tissue from his left index fingertip.
An employee was installing a 14-inch pipe when they fell from an I-beam to the concrete floor below. The employee sustained a brain bleed.
An employee was standing on an extension ladder tightening a screw. The employee fell off the ladder to the ground and broke their left ankle. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was operating a skid steer. He was loading sand into the large hopper when he brought the bucket down and his foot was pinched between the arms of the crossbar and the frame of the cab. As the arms continued to come down, they pulled his foot and ankle over the edge of the cab, resulting in a broken leg.

On March 18, 2025, an employee was working from an 8-foot A-frame ladder while using a battery-powered impact wrench to break bolts loose from a pipe in the ceiling. As they descended the ladder, the employee fell to the ground, resulting in a brain bleed and cut/scrapes on their hands.
An employee fell from the roof of a residential home to the ground and was hospitalized with a broken left leg. Fall protection was not used at the time.

An employee was unbinding a load of guardrail. The employee went to release a levered binder and the binder struck him in the lower right leg. The employee was hospitalized with a fractured tibia and fibula that required surgery.

An employee was throwing trash into a dumpster while he was inside a cage on a forklift. The employee lost his balance and fell 3 feet to the concrete ground. The employee sustained fractured vertebrae and a scrape on their left elbow.
An employee was climbing a ladder to access a roof. They missed a rung and fell 18 feet to the ground. The employee was hospitalized with a back injury.

An employee was signaling a crane to hoist a concrete wall panel when they were struck by the wall panel and fell over another wall panel. The employee struck the ground and was hospitalized with fractures to their lower left leg, three right ribs, and a contusion.
An employee was installing gutters from a ladder, about 14 feet above the ground. The employee fell from the ladder to the ground, hitting their head and suffering a forehead fracture.

An employee was clearing snow and ice in the lot around a shop. He was working between a pickup truck and a flatbed truck, pushing snow off the trucks so he could move them to clear the area around them. He slipped on a patch of snow-covered ice, fell, and landed on his back. He suffered broken vertebrae.

An employee was building a sea wall. One of the sea wall panels weighing 2,250 pounds fell from waist high on top of him. The employee sustained fractures to his shoulder, collarbone, arm, ribs, and pelvis.
An employee was painting a wall from a elevated scissor lift and fell from the lift to the ground below. The employee sustained a concussion and was hospitalized.

On March 21, 2025, an employee was notching out 2x6 wood blocking with a handheld router when his left hand slipped and the router lacerated his right index and middle fingers. The employee was hospitalized and required stitches.
An employee unhooked the winch cable to a dumpster. The dumpster dropped onto their right foot, causing fractures and a laceration.

On March 21, 2025, at approximately 10:15 AM, an employee was removing an electrical feeder wire from rigid conduit using a tugger/puller. One end of a rope was attached to the wire being pulled and the other end was wound around a powered capstan (cylinder/spindle). While pulling the wire, the employee's gloved right hand became caught in the rope and was pulled into the capstan, crushing their forearm. The employee was hospitalized with fractures to their right radius and ulna, as well as the amputation of their little finger.
An employee was descending a ladder when they fell 6 feet to the ground. The employee was hospitalized with head and neck injuries.
An employee was working from a scissor lift when the lift tipped over. The employee fell to the ground, sustaining broken ribs and other internal injuries.
An employee was using a table saw to cut a splicer piece when the metal kicked back and the employee's finger contacted the saw blade. The employee sustained a finger amputation.

An employee was performing excavation work to expose a 12-foot water pipe. A large clod of dirt estimated to be 3 to 4 feet in size dislodged from a spoil pile and fell, striking his right leg. The impact caused the employee to lose consciousness momentarily. The employee was hospitalized with a fractured tibia and fibula and required surgery.
An employee was walking on the dirt ground at a construction site when he rolled his right ankle due to uneven ground, resulting in a torn ligament.
An employee was removing a garage door. The door spring was under tension when it released, striking the employee's head and arm. The employee sustained a head injury and a fractured arm.

Employees were using a crane to move pieces of an air handler off a roof. They were lowering a sand wheel with the crane. When the sand wheel touched the ground, the injured employee went to stabilize it. The steel cable used to rig the sand wheel moved and caught his thumb, causing an amputation.

An employee was installing steel beams and fell approximately 12 feet from a beam to the ground. The employee landed on tools and suffered a traumatic brain injury, fractured vertebrae, and pelvic fractures. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee sustained chemical burns on the lower parts of both legs after standing in concrete.

An employee was hauling hot mix asphalt in a tandem dump truck. He was cleaning up buildup around the latch that holds the tailgate pin and using a scraper to wedge the tailgate open. The pin came down on his left middle finger, resulting in a tissue amputation and loss of the fingernail.

An employee was looking at a leak in an air conditioner coil when they stepped through the ceiling and fell approximately 10 to 11 feet. The employee was hospitalized with fractures to four ribs, their L1 vertebra, and their pelvis.

On March 24, 2025, an employee was in an aerial bucket pulling a fiber optic internet cable through tree limbs from a residence to the communication pole. The employee contacted energized power lines and sustained electrical burns to both palms and knuckles and burns to his left forearm.

An employee was part of a team that was moving a pre-fab wall panel. When other team members let go of the panel, the employee's finger became caught between the wall panel and the concrete floor resulting in an amputation.
An employee was wetting a concrete slab when they fell backward off the stairs to the ground, landing on their back. The employee's back was fractured.
An employee had been chipping out concrete from the outside curve of a bridge. The employee fell approximately 15 feet from the bridge to the ground. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was working approximately 20 feet in the air. They were cutting and laying oriented strand board on the deck of a 3-story building. The employee fell from the roof to the ground and was hospitalized with fractures to their wrists, contusions over the right side of their body, and right shoulder pain.

An employee placed 6-inch wooden planks over metal trusses to establish a walking/working surface. The employee lost his footing, fell off a plank, and struck the metal deck. He went through the metal deck and landed on the ground approximately 10 feet below. The employee sustained a right elbow contusion and a bruised kidney. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was using a crowbar to slide a forklift s forks into a new position. The fork popped loose, causing the crowbar to slip out from under the fork. The employee lost their balance and fell to the ground, fracturing their femur.

An employee was working to remove the auger of a boring machine from a new water pipe. The boring machine bound up and rolled which pinched the employee between the roll cage bar of the boring machine and the trench box. The employee sustained pelvic and lower extremity fractures with internal injuries.

The injured employee was team lifting a steel tube from an A-frame dolly using the shoulder-to shoulder method with another employee. They lifted one end of the tube so the A-frame could be wheeled out of the way by a third employee. Once the dolly was clear, they lowered the tube down on top of another tube. After setting the tube down, it slipped off the lower tube and fell. The moving tube pulled the injured employee's glove and his left middle fingertip was caught between the two tubes. The employee sustained an avulsion to their finger.

An employee was standing next to a trench box waiting to hook up a steel plate for removal. The plate shifted and the employee fell into the trench, resulting in broken ribs, a bruised lung, and multiple contusions.
An employee was welding a beam when they fell 12 feet from a scissor lift to the ground. The employee sustained fractures to their face, thumb, and both wrists.
An employee was helping to remove a skylight from a roof. The skylight got hooked on his harness and pulled him off the roof to the ground. The employee was hospitalized with back fractures.

On March 26, 2025, an employee was operating a forklift. They were passing a stationary skid steer when their left foot contacted the skid steer, resulting in a crushed left ankle. The employee was hospitalized and required surgery.
An employee was setting up traffic control devices on the interstate. A vehicle entered the traffic control zone and struck the employee on the left leg, fracturing their tibia and fibula.

Employees were loading an I-beam using a crane and a scissor lift. The crane lifted the I-beam to where the employees were working in the scissor lift. One employee exited the lift basket to guide the I-beam into position. The employee went to use a strap to position the I-beam on the chamber by pulling the I-beam toward him and getting it into position. The injured employee was in the lift with his hand on the I-beam, and when the I-beam moved, his hand was caught between the I-beam and the scissor lift. The employee sustained an amputation of their left ring fingertip.

An employee was using a compound miter saw to cut 3/8" molding. As the saw slowed, the saw caught onto a piece of molding and pulled the employee's left middle finger into the blade, amputating the fingertip.

An employee was making repairs to a fire sprinkler system. The piping in the system broke and caused the employee to lose balance and fall from a ladder to the concrete floor below. The employee sustained injuries to the head, face, and neck.

On 3/27/2025, at approximately 8:00 AM, an employee was dismounting a mobile excavator after fueling it with diesel. He lost his balance, slipped, and fell approximately three feet, striking his rib cage against a metal step on the excavator. The employee sustained multiple left rib fractures and a partially collapsed left lung.
An employee was installing a metal roof when they fell through a fiberglass skylight and landed on the warehouse floor 24 feet below. The employee sustained bruises.
An employee was pouring concrete. The hose clogged and then whipped around and struck the employee in the abdomen. The employee sustained liver damage and internal bleeding.

An employee was removing rigging at the top of a concrete form. The form collapsed and the employee fell with the form to the ground. The form landed on the employee's leg. The employee sustained fractures to their jaw and femur.

On March 28, 2025, an employee working as a machine operator was changing the teeth on a milling drum. He was using the tooth extractor when his left index finger became caught between the drum and the extractor. The employee's fingertip was amputated.

An employee was cutting pipe with a cutoff saw when the saw blade became pinched. When the employee pulled the saw out of the cut, the blade came back and struck their lip, causing a wound to the face.

An employee was finishing concrete with a float. He pulled the handle of the float up and it struck an overhead power line. The employee was shocked and lost consciousness. He also sustained burns to the face and left foot.

On March 31, 2025, an employee was on a ladder trimming vegetation using a pole saw. The ladder became unstable and the employee fell to the ground, resulting in multiple fractures to the left wrist. The employee was hospitalized for surgery.

Employees were setting braces on a vertical wall. They had it rigged up using a jib pole attachment on a front-end loader. They secured a brace and an employee went up a ladder to disconnect the rigging from the hook. The injured employee was holding the ladder. The jib pole attachment (estimated to weigh 2,000 pounds) detached from the loader, struck the injured employee, and pinned him against the ladder. The employee was hospitalized with multiple injuries including a punctured lung, fractures to his collarbone, arm, and femur, and injuries to his hip and leg.

An employee was working 8 feet above the ground while installing sheet metal as a roof over a pathway. The employee secured one side of the sheet metal and stepped over it to secure the other side. He fell through the sheet metal, hitting the ground on his left side and arm. The employee fractured ribs and a clavicle.
An employee had been framing walls. He was using a nail gun to nail a sill for the windows when the nail gun bounced and nailed his leg.
An employee was installing new shingles on a 2-story residential roof and fell off the backside of the roof to the ground, sustaining head and hip injuries.

On April 1, 2025, an employee was setting trusses. When he repositioned himself on another area of the structure, he stepped on an unsecured truss and fell 11 feet and 6 inches to the concrete surface, and sustained head and brain injuries. Fall protection was in place at the time.

An employee was on the roof installing sheathing on wooden trusses. The employee fell approximately 16-18 feet and landed on the concrete ground, striking his head. The fall resulted in fractured bones in the chest, a fractured skull, and fractured ribs.

An employee was changing a manual steel thumb on an excavator. When the thumb was disconnected, he lost his balance and fell from the excavator bucket he had been standing on. The thumb then pinned his left foot and knee, causing injuries to the foot and the knee that resulted in swelling and ligament damage.
An employee was installing a safety rail on the third floor and fell 23 feet. The employee sustained a neck fracture.

On April 1, 2025, a crane/hoist operator was working to dislodge a hook from a wheel. The remote controls for the crane activated and caused the crane to move. The employee's right index and middle fingers became caught between the wheel and the hook, resulting in an amputation to her index fingertip and lacerations to her middle finger.

The injured employee was setting up tie-down straps to secure a load on a trailer for transport. Another employee was operating a forklift and set a pallet of material down at a staging area near the trailer. As the forklift reversed, its left rear tire struck and ran over the injured employee's legs, resulting in broken bones in the right leg and bruising on the left leg.

Two employees were lifting a radio antenna up the tower using a winch when the rope got bound up in the spool of the winch. They were repositioning the spool of rope when the winch began to take the rope more quickly and pulled the injured employee's left hand that was holding the rope into the winch. The employee's left middle and ring fingers were injured and the little finger was broken.
An employee was climbing a ladder when the ladder broke and folded up. The employee fell and sustained fractured ribs and a punctured lung.

An employee was installing elevator rails when they fell from their ladder to the concrete floor. The employee sustained a scalp laceration, a fractured left fibula, and compression fractures to their T4 and T5 vertebrae.

An employee was part of an electrical crew attempting to "cant"/twist a 55-foot steel pole into the ground using a twisting tool (a 2-inch choker strap and a steel bar). While twisting the tool, it slipped and the injured employee fell to the ground, fracturing their left ankle. The employee was hospitalized.

On April 2, 2025, an employee was applying stucco/drywall when he fell from the scaffolding. The employee was hospitalized with a dislocated finger and multiple fractures to his left elbow that required surgery.

An employee was using a pry bar to remove a component from a water pump when the component shifted and the pry bar pinned his finger against the pump. The employee sustained a lacerated and broken left ring finger.

An employee was directing a co-worker who was removing rebar from a semi-truck trailer when the rebar caught his pant leg and he fell 4 feet from the trailer to the asphalt. The employee sustained a laceration to his left leg and fractures to his elbow, arm, and left hip.

An employee was unloading glass panels from a delivery truck and riding the lift gate down with a cart of the panels. The material shifted when the lift gate reached the ground and the glass panels fell onto his right foot. The employee sustained three fractures to his foot.
An employee was taking ductwork from the penthouse machine room down to the freight elevator level. They fell down stairs and were hospitalized with a brain bleed and a skull fracture.

An employee was using a 20-foot ladder to access the roof when he began moving the ladder, lost his balance, and fell 18 feet to the ground. The employee was hospitalized with fractures to his back, pelvis, and five ribs. He also sustained internal bleeding, a kidney injury, and nerve damage to a leg.
An employee was decking a home when a 2-inch roofing staple was discharged from a pneumatic staple gun into his right knee. The employee was hospitalized and required surgery to remove the staple.
On April 3, 2025, an employee was throwing scrap drywall out of an opening in the second floor and fell to the ground. The employee was hospitalized with a fractured left tibia.
An employee was moving an A-frame cart loaded with two pieces of stone. The cart tipped over and struck his lower left leg, breaking it and causing other injuries. He was hospitalized.
An employee was terminating feeders inside distribution panels at a new construction site when an arc flash occurred and they sustained burns.

An employee was delivering construction materials and was trying to loosen a tie down on the back of the truck. When the strap came loose it caused the ratchet bar to jolt forward pinching their left little finger between the ratchet bar and forks on the back of the truck and resulting in a fingertip amputation.

On April 7, 2025, an employee was cutting a fitting off fuel oil piping using a portable band saw. The fitting caught in the jaw of the blade and rotated his finger into the blade. The employee sustained a partial amputation to his left third finger, an avulsion, and a fracture.
A subcontractor employee was installing roof trusses from the third floor of a building when they fell and were hospitalized with a severe injury to their head and back.

An employee was picking up traffic barrels while standing on a moving flatbed trailer. When the vehicle made a U-turn, the employee lost his balance and fell onto the freeway pavement. The employee sustained a fracture to the back of the skull and a brain bleed.

An employee was standing on the back of a paving machine and preparing to pave. A roller was driving toward the paving machine and pinned the employee against the back of the paver, crushing his right leg. His stomach was impaled by the screw bar handle of the paving machine. The employee sustained a laceration to the abdomen and an amputation to the left leg.

An employee was releasing a chain binder that was securing a spooler on a trailer when it released unexpectedly and struck him in the lower right leg. The employee sustained a fractured right leg and was hospitalized, requiring surgery.
An employee was using a circular saw to cut a 2x4 when the saw kicked back and amputated his left index finger.
An employee was on a roof 20 feet above the lower level moving roofing tile bundles when he fell to the ground. The employee sustained a fractured wrist.

An employee was walking on metal decking on the second floor when it gave way and they fell 15 feet to the ground. The employee sustained fractures to their right tibia and fibula just above the ankle.
An employee got into a physical altercation with another employee at the job site and he sustained a fractured jaw. He was hospitalized and required surgery.
An employee was positioning inspection platform brackets on the forks of a forklift when a bracket moved and pinched the employee's right third finger, resulting in a partial amputation.

At about 12:05 p.m. on April 8, 2025, while performing material handling tasks on jack-up scaffolding, an employee of [EMPLOYER] was walking along the scaffold's inner-face walk board when the walk board became dislodged from its holding flange. The employee fell to the ground and suffered abrasions to the right arm and the left side of the chest. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was working from an extension ladder to install an exterior receptable outlet on the soffit at a newly constructed home. They fell from the ladder to the ground and the ladder ended up on the ground also. The employee was hospitalized with a fractured femur and required surgery.

An employee fell through a warehouse skylight, landing about 20 feet below on the ground and on equipment in the warehouse. The employee suffered a laceration to the upper leg, as well as a broken arm and wrist.
An employee was mixing grout with a portable handheld drill. The employee's sleeve became entangled in the drill bit, resulting in an amputation to the employee's left thumb.

An employee was using a grinder machine to cut through a section of concrete flooring at the job site. The grinder shifted due to uneven surface resistance and the rotating blade lacerated the inner side of his right foot, causing a wound about 4 inches long and inch deep.

Two employees were standing next to a 2 1/2-foot-deep excavation when its edge collapsed. Both employees fell into the excavation; one landed on the other's upward-pointing knee and suffered broken ribs and a lung injury.

An employee was walking around the site, inspecting the progress of a newly started project. The job was in the foundation stage and the upright rebar of the footings had just started to get placed and tied into the footers. The employee stepped over one of the footings and tripped. He landed on an upright rebar that punctured his lower jaw.
An employee was holding a pipe that was being cut with a gas-powered cutoff saw. The sawblade broke into pieces, one of which lacerated the employee's left thigh and required surgery.
An employee was jack hammering the concrete pad below the bridge bearing. The bridge bearing shifted and fell onto the employee's left thumb, resulting in amputation of the thumb tip.
An excavator bucket fell, bounced, and struck an employee's leg, injuring it. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was climbing a utility pole to conduct maintenance work and made contact with the electrical line. The employee was hospitalized for electric shock with burns to his right hand and wrist. Personal protective equipment was not worn at the time.

Two steel plates (5 feet by 10 feet by 3/16 inch) had been rigged using a shackle, sling, and tagline, then positioned vertically at the ground level by a crane. An employee detached the rigging from the crane hook and two employees were stabilizing the load as it lowered to a 45-degree angle. As the plates were being lowered, they shifted and caught the left foot of one of the two employees against stacked plates. The employee's left tibia and fibula were broken.

An employee was in the basket of an aerial lift preparing to install glass on a 14th-floor hoist deck. His right foot got tangled on the lift's ladder while exiting the basket, causing him to fall and land on his left side, striking his upper body and right arm on the outrigger. The employee was hospitalized due to four fractured ribs and a fractured right wrist.

An employee was conducting a pressure test of sewer laterals. The pressure gauge dropped to 0 PSI. The employee checked the pipe and wiggled it. A 6 to 8 inch pipe shot out of the ground and struck the employee's jaw/chin. The employee sustained a fracture to the jaw and a laceration to the bottom of the chin. The employee was hospitalized.
Two employees were working in a 6- to 8-foot trench when it collapsed on them. One employee suffered broken ribs and broken lower-back vertebra; the other employee suffered a broken femur.
Employees were standing under the bridge as it had started raining. An employee leaned on a concrete barrier and it fell over onto their left leg, crushing it.

At about 6:45 a.m. on April 10th, 2025, an employee was lining up a pallet on a mixer palletizer. While he was lifting and placing the pallet on the palletizer, it came down on his right middle finger and crushed it against the machine. He suffered an amputation to the fingertip.
An employee was walking across a roof when it collapsed. He fell through to the ground below and suffered a broken collarbone, broken ribs, a fractured skull, a brain injury, and a collapsed lung.

A construction crew was working on a bore section that crossed under an interstate. One of them was crossing the interstate, and was in the center median next to a cable barrier, when a tire came off a trailer being hauled by a truck and struck his left side. He suffered fractures to his leg and left hip, as well as lacerations to his body and lower abdomen. He was hospitalized, requiring surgery.

On April 11, 2025, two employees were sliding an I-beam so that its end would meet another I-beam. One employee's left ring finger was pinched between the two I-beams, and the fingertip was amputated.

An employee was about four or five steps up an A-frame ladder, pulling wire through a wall, while another employee held the ladder. The employee lost his balance and fell from the ladder onto his feet, suffering a broken tibia.

At 9:00 a.m. on April 11, 2025, a framer was in a manlift about 15 feet in the air. He was moving from the manlift onto a roof when he slipped and fell, landing on the ground. He suffered a compound fracture to the left wrist and a broken nose.

An employee was scraping the roof of an auditorium at a middle school. They were standing on a two-tier portable scaffold on wheels. The scaffold moved and the employee fell approximately 15 feet to the ground below, resulting in head trauma.

An employee was moving material on a roof. The employee fell 14 feet from the roof to the top floor of the building beneath, striking the concrete floor. He sustained a partial thickness injury to the back of his head requiring staples, fractured left ribs, and a spinal injury requiring surgery.
A concrete form fell over and pinned an employee's leg to the ground. The employee was hospitalized with a broken tibia.

An employee was moving a piece of precast concrete to center it on a pallet. His right middle finger was pinched between the precast and the pallet, resulting in a fracture of the distal phalanx and a partial finger amputation.
On April 14, 2025, an employee was hooking a small dump trailer to a ball hitch. The employee's middle fingertip was caught between the ball and the hitch and amputated.

An employee was pressure washing grease on a low-sloped roof when their fall protection lanyard caught on the roof, causing them to trip and drop the pressure washer wand. The spray hit the employee's right leg and thigh, resulting in an abrasion and injected water below the surface of the skin.
An employee was cutting trim with a miter saw when the blade kicked back and contacted their thumb, resulting in an amputation.

An employee was on an 8-foot stepladder pulling electrical wiring. The wire broke, causing the employee to lose balance and fall to the ground. The employee sustained a broken ankle and compression fractures to their lower back.

An employee was disconnecting and unscrewing a spinner and a J-bolt from a suspended 80- to 100-pound steel waler. The waler slipped and the employee's left thumb was pinched between the waler's flange and the J-bolt, resulting in amputation of the thumb tip.

Two employees were erecting a hydraulic mast climber scaffold with an eight-foot extension work platform. They erected it to the maximum height of 30 feet and were lowering the scaffold to install ties. While lowering the scaffold, there was a malfunction and one of the sides of the scaffold did not catch, causing it to come down quickly. A safety mechanism caused it to catch, but the force caused the other tower to tip over. The employees were ejected from the platform but were tied off to the guardrails/hoists above them using self-retracting lanyards. Employee 1 was hospitalized with bruises, lacerations, and a concussion. Employee 2 was hospitalized with bruising, facial lacerations, and a shoulder injury.

An employee was performing roofing activities on a commercial roof. As the employee walked to the ladder to exit the roof for lunch, they stepped on a piece of insulation that hung over the roof and fell approximately 17 feet to the ground. The employee was hospitalized with a wedge compression fracture to the L2 and T12 vertebrae and traumatic rupture of a lumbar intervertebral disc.

An employee was setting a portion of trench drain by hand. The piece was approximately 30 inches long and weighed 50 pounds. The employee lost his grip and his little finger was pinched between the piece and another piece that was already set in place, resulting in a fingertip amputation including bone.

An employee was working at the stair tower and was struck by a 4 x 8 sheet of 5/8" plywood that a gust of wind blew airborne. The employee temporarily lost consciousness and was hospitalized due to fractures to his face and skull.

On April 15, 2025, an employee was operating a cut-off saw to cut a section of 12" precast concrete storm pipe in preparation for installation and suffered a cut to the front of the neck. The employee was hospitalized.

Employees were laying asphalt paving on a highway. The injured employee was walking beside the paver machine with his hand on top of the road widener extension. The extension was lowered and his finger was pinched between the machine and a steel guardrail along the side of the highway. As a result, the injured employee sustained an amputation of his right middle fingertip.
An employee was working on a roof when they fell to the ground, resulting in an injury to their left foot and shin.

Two employees were driving a water truck pulling a trailer on the sloped shoulder within the barricade of a work zone when the truck and the trailer rolled over. One employee sustained a broken femur and was hospitalized. The second employee sustained contusions to the lower back left side and left forearm and was not hospitalized.
An employee was walking through a building when they tripped on a 6-inch-long wire and fell, resulting in a fractured knee.
An employee was lifting a torque tube with an all terrain forklift when he struck a powerline and and sustained an electrical shock.

The injured employee was helping another employee put a clamp on an I-beam that was attached to a crane. When the crane began to lift the load, the I-beam tipped to the left and caught the injured employee's left leg against another I-beam. The employee was hospitalized with crush injuries to his left tibia and fibula and required surgery.

An employee was refueling a gas-powered mobile air compressor when it caught on fire. The employee caught on fire from the fireball and suffered third-degree burns to the left arm and lesser burns to the right arm.

An employee was working from inside a boom lift installing screws into sheet metal siding. The employee reached over the top rail of the lift and fell approximately 15 feet to the concrete below, resulting in a fractured leg. Fall protection was not utilized at the time.
An employee was using a chainsaw to cut plastic pipe in a hole. The chainsaw kicked back and lacerated the employee's chest.

An employee working from an 8-foot A-frame ladder was running wire inside a ceiling space. The garage door activated via remote and pinned the employee against the ceiling space. The employee sustained fractures to his ribs and back.
An employee was using a circular saw to cut wood for concrete formwork and cut his right thigh.

An employee was patching a reinforced concrete pipe that was 36 inches in diameter and 8 feet long. The employee was on a patch line with his right hand placed on the outside of the pipe to use it for leverage. When the pipe transport dropped off the next pipe, it rolled and crushed his right hand between the two pipes, resulting in amputation of the ring fingertip.
An employee was descending a ladder when he missed a step. He reached out to catch himself on a wall and his left middle finger was fractured by the hard surface.
An employee was speaking to a concrete truck driver when an air plug popped off the concrete truck and struck the employee in the head, resulting in a laceration. The employee was hospitalized.

On April 18, 2025, at 9:15 a.m., an employee was on a roof getting ready to stock materials. He lifted a plywood cover laying over a roof opening and he fell approximately 15 feet through the opening, landing on a scissor lift below. The employee suffered fractures to his ribs and pelvis.
On April 18, 2025, an employee was entering an excavator cabin when they fell to the ground and broke a hip.
An employee was assisting with backing up a stake body truck to the loading dock. They got pinned between the lift gate of the truck and the loading dock door. The employee sustained fractured ribs.

An employee was pulling electrical wire while standing on a 6-foot step ladder. The rope used to pull the electrical wire broke, causing the employee to fall backward to the floor. The employee's knee was fractured.

An employee was on a 12-foot ladder working above a drop ceiling when he lost balance and fell about 10 feet to the ground, landing on his feet. The employee sustained a Lisfranc fracture and dislocation to their left foot. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was framing a single-story home when the board he was walking on broke and he fell through the trusses to the concrete floor. He was hospitalized with injuries to his head and ribs.

The injured employee was assisting with backfilling an excavation. The employee was kneeling on the pipe with both knees and was holding a piece of plywood while their right hand sat on the second pipe next to the hole. While the excavator was backfilling the trench he was shaking the bucket to allow the dirt to come out. A piece of concrete fell out of the bucket and struck the back of the employee's right hand, causing a displaced fracture to the metacarpal bone of the index finger, a fracture to the metacarpal bone of the middle finger, and a laceration.
An employee was operating a folding machine when three fingers on their right hand were crushed. The middle finger was amputated to the first knuckle.

On April 21, 2025, at around 6:15 PM, an employee was working on a dual-tank asphalt distributor truck with reports of a clogged A/C line. When the return plug was removed, hot liquid asphalt projected out of the drain hole and onto the employee. The employee was hospitalized with burns to parts of his face, neck, and both arms.

An employee was checking the grade of a pipe invert in a new precast concrete inlet box and determined that it needed to be trimmed. The employee was cutting the box with a demolition saw when the blade bound up and the saw kicked back, severely lacerating his right cheek.

An employee was helping to dismantle a mobile crawler crane. Employees were separating boom sections. When the last pin was hammered out, the 40-foot boom section dropped 4-5 inches onto the injured employee's left foot. All five toes were amputated and the employee was hospitalized for surgery.

An employee was standing on the top of a 6-foot rolling scaffold putting tongue and groove 1 x 6 boards on the bottom of a covered patio when he fell and landed on the concrete patio. The employee suffered head trauma and broken bones in his back and wrist.

Two employees were loading a flatbed truck using forklifts. One employee placed a load on the truck and was backing up their lift when one of the forks dislodged from the carriage, bounced on the ground, and struck the injured employee's leg, fracturing it.

On April 22, 2025, at approximately 6:35 p.m., an employee was working on a turnaround project. The crew was venting off nitrogen from an 18-inch pipeline into a 2-inch silencer vessel. The 18-inch pipe was pressurized with nitrogen gas at approximately 1200 psig. The silencer suddenly ruptured and its internal components were blown away. The shell of the silencer struck downward, landed on the employee's left hand due to high pressure, and lacerated the employee's left index finger resulting in amputation. The employee's left wrist was also broken.
An employee was descending a step ladder when his foot got caught on edge of step and he fell from the ladder to the guardrail below. The employee was hospitalized with broken ribs.

An employee was using a sledgehammer to drive stakes into the ground to secure PVC conduit. The employee's right index finger was caught between the pipe being driven and the sledgehammer, resulting in a compound fracture of the distal phalanges.

On April 23, 2025, an employee removed the pin on a Kelly bar to remove it from a drill rig. The auger was lifted to remove the Kelly bar, and the employee's left ring finger was caught in the pin hole. The employee suffered a partial fingertip amputation and was hospitalized.

An employee was working on a roof when he fell through the roof's paneling. He struck a full-sized refrigerator on the way down and landed on the concrete. He sustained a broken collarbone, fractured ribs on his right side, and a cut on his face.
An employee slipped and fell off a gang wall, landing on the ground 12 feet below. The employee's leg was broken in two places. Fall protection was not utilized at the time.
An employee was cutting pipe with a circular saw when the saw kicked back and and struck the employee's face, lacerating his face, lips, teeth and surrounding areas.

An employee was walking backward while assisting with the removal of a 24-foot aluminum walk board and fell approximately 18 feet from the wooden deck to the ground. The employee sustained head, hand and facial injuries.

An employee was installing a metal plug into a machine. He was using a wrench to turn the metal plug a quarter turn more when the round plug weighing approximately 2 pounds failed and blew off from pressure, striking the employee in the face. The employee sustained facial lacerations and a fractured jaw.

An employee was on an 8-foot step ladder using a "fish stick" to pull cable for a fire alarm at a school. He was on the sixth rung when he fell to the floor. He was hospitalized with fractures to his back and hip.
A power broom sweeper truck backed into an employee in a roadway construction area. The employee suffered a broken left shoulder blade and a broken left orbital bone.
An employee set up a ladder to investigate a noise onsite. The employee fell from the ladder to the ground and sustained fractures to his left leg and right foot.

Employees were installing a large metal pipe into a pipe rack in the battery plant using a crane. The injured employee was working in a scissor lift approximately 24 feet above the ground. As the pipe was lifted, it struck the injured employee and caused three rib fractures and chest trauma.

The injured employee was prepping for a new framing panel. An air hose wrapped around the employee's leg and caused him to trip and fall. He struck a framing stud and then the ground. The employee sustained a bloody nose and a hip injury requiring hospitalization.

Two employees were working on a battery storage unit when an arc flash occurred. Employee 1 was hospitalized with third-degree burns to his face and left ear, his left arm and hand, and the fingertips on his right hand. Employee 2 sustained first-degree burns to their face, and first- and second-degree burns to their hands. Employee 2 was not hospitalized.

On April 26, 2025, an employee was assisting with a concrete column pour when a 2-inch by 30-foot pipe, which weighed approximately 80 to 100 pounds, moved out of the cage and fell. The pipe struck his right foot and he was hospitalized with a fracture to his right little toe.

At approximately 10:55 a.m. on 4/27/2025, an employee was reversing the saw cutting machine toward the test pit. While stepping backward, he fell into the test pit. The saw cutting machine also continued rolling into the pit and landed on him. The employee sustained fractured ribs.

An employee was welding a 12-inch steam line while standing on top of a boiler. While descending from the boiler, the employee lost his footing and slipped off a 6-foot A-frame ladder and his left foot struck the floor. The employee sustained a fractured left heel.
An employee was tying down to an anchor when they slipped and fell from the roof to the ground. The employee sustained a broken leg and was hospitalized.
An employee was manipulating the tailgate on a truck and crushed a finger, resulting in amputation.
An employee was cutting water-damaged floorboards on the first floor. They stepped on a rotted floorboard and fell three feet into a crawl space. The employee sustained five broken ribs.

An employee was using a saw to make cuts into concrete masonry units. The saw caught fire, which caused the employee to drop the saw and the gas cap broke. The gas spilled partially onto the employee and the fire spread to their clothing. The employee suffered burns to the waist area and was hospitalized.

An employee was in a bucket truck trimming trees from power lines using a hydraulic pole saw. While cutting a tree limb, the limb contacted the power line and the employee's left shoulder, resulting in an electric shock to the shoulder. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was working on electrical wiring in the garage of a new home. The employee fell from a 6-8' step ladder and landed on the concrete floor. The employee sustained fractures to their jaw, cheekbone, and right wrist.

An employee was troubleshooting connectors for computer controls and was kneeling down on the ground to disconnect a pin cable connection. He reached forward and felt his lower back pop/lock and could not move to a standing position. The employee was hospitalized for a lower back sprain/strain.
An employee was working on top of a service truck when they slipped and fell approximately 5 feet to the ground. The employee sustained fractured ribs.

An employee was resetting an air handling unit in a mechanical room on a roof. He completed the task and exited the mechanical room, stepping up onto a 14-inch high roof expansion that had a metal top cap near the leading edge. He slipped off the top cap and fell approximately 18.5 feet to the courtyard below. The employee sustained fractured ribs and a back injury.

An employee contacted a live power line and the case of a transformer at the same time and sustained an electrical shock that resulted in the amputation of both hands. Personal protective equipment (rubberized gloves) was not worn at the time.

Two employees were installing conduit for electrical service. The two-pole electrical service disconnect fell onto both employees. One employee was treated and released. The second employee was hospitalized for a knee injury and ligament damage.

An employee was offloading portable power distribution unit (PDU) equipment from a delivery truck. The PDU was being lowered on the box truck's tailgate lift when one of the PDU's wheels rolled forward. The unit fell to the ground, toppled over, and struck the employee. The employee was hospitalized with injuries to the right side of their body including their shoulder and hip, and injuries to their left elbow. The employee's hip was fractured.
While wiring a low-voltage tunnel controller, loose wires came in contact with a high-voltage breaker, causing an electric spark that burned the employee's right hand.

An employee was installing gutters while working on a roof. He untied himself to descend and slipped on water that was on the roof. He fell off the roof and landed in a dumpster. The employee sustained fractures to his shoulder and elbow.

An employee was working from a manlift putting the perimeter plywood decking on top of the joists on top of the walls. The employee climbed from the manlift onto the decking. He lost his footing and fell through the floor joists approximately 14 feet and 8 inches to the concrete below. The employee sustained a concussion, a ruptured spleen, and broken ribs.

An employee was preparing to work on a rooftop fan unit. The employee was slowing down the fan blades when the belt pulled the employee's left little finger around the pulley, resulting in amputation of the little and ring fingertips.

An employee was rigging a portable welding machine to the lifting hook of an excavator. Their right hand became caught between the excavator bucket and the welding machine. The employee sustained a laceration to their hand and a fracture/dislocation to their middle finger.
An employee was ascending a ladder so he could secure it. The ladder slipped out from under him, causing him to fall off the ladder and fracture his left wrist.

A skid steer operator was attaching a skid steer's bucket loaded with concrete (estimated to be up to 500 pounds) to a machine. The injured employee was reaching in front of the bucket to move pieces of broken concrete when the bucket fell on his right arm, catching it between the bucket and concrete. The employee sustained a fractured arm and thumb, a laceration to the index finger, and an avulsion to their middle finger.

An employee was stacking concrete blocks that were going to be picked up by a skid steer. The employee went to move a block that was leaning against the stack. The block landed next to the stack and the employee's right hand was caught between two blocks. The employee's index finger was partially amputated and the first knuckle was fractured.

On April 30, 2025, at about 1:41 PM, a temporary employee was on the second floor of an apartment parking garage when they fell into an unguarded elevator shaft and landed on the first floor. The employee sustained fractures to his legs, arms, head, back, and neck requiring hospitalization. Fall protection was not in place at the time.

On April 30, 2025, an employee was installing solar panels on the roof of a residential home. His fall protection anchor failed, and he fell from the roof to the ground. The employee sustained fractures to their C6 and C7 vertebrae, collapsed lungs, a heart injury, and he was paralyzed from the chest down.
An employee was walking on the ramp when he misstepped and fell to the same level. The employee sustained fractures to his elbow and rib, and a shoulder injury.

An employee was inspecting buckets on a bucket elevator/conveyor and manually moving the conveyor when an unidentified item/part fell from a height and struck their right arm. The employee was hospitalized with a fractured arm.
On May 1, 2025, an employee was cutting a hanger with a band saw when their hand slipped and their left index finger contacted the blade. The employee sustained a fingertip amputation.

On May 1, 2025, an employee was cutting a pipe while working inside a trench that was 20' long x 3.5' deep x 4.5' wide. A shaft of dirt fell onto the employee's leg. The employee sustained an injury to their anterior tibial artery.
An employee was changing out the auger on a pressure digger when they sustained a partial amputation of their right index and middle fingers.
An employee was conducting a roofing estimate when they slipped and fell off the roof to the ground. The employee was hospitalized with a fractured vertebra.
An employee was entering an HVAC plenum when their left thumb was caught in the door and amputated between the nailbed and the knuckle.
An employee was loading a spool of wire into the bed of a pickup truck when the spool started to fall and the employee went to catch it. The spool crushed his left ring finger.
An employee was moving an electrical line out of the way of a reversing trailer when they were shocked by the electrical line. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was changing the blade on a tractor and holding the blade up with one hand. She twisted her body to reach for a link sitting on the tractor when she felt a pop in her lower back. The employee sustained a burst fracture of her L4 vertebra.

A carpenter was tied-off on a baker scaffold and framing an addition to a local school. The employee climbed into the trusses to move the scaffold closer to himself. The scaffold tipped over and pulled the employee down to the concrete ground below. The employee was hospitalized with a broken leg.
An employee was inspecting a roof for damage when his ladder slipped and he fell approximately 6-8 feet to the ground, landing on his heels. The employee was hospitalized with fractures to both feet.
An employee was walking when they tripped on a piece of PVC pipe and fell to the ground. The employee sustained two fractures to their knee cap.
An employee was near a concrete pump truck when it made contact with electrical transmission lines. The employee was shocked, suffering entry and exit wounds (with burns).
An employee was struck by an excavator bucket and caught between the bucket and a stone pile. The employee sustained a fractured left arm and lacerations.

Employees were organizing material in the laydown area. Four employees were lifting a 4 x 4 concrete form weighing approximately 187 pounds when the injured employee experienced back pain. The employee sustained an L4 vertebra fracture.
An employee was performing electrical work when his left arm was caught by a cable/wire pulling machine and pulled in. The employee sustained two fractures to the arm and amputation of two fingers.
An employee was painting from a ladder when he fell to the ground. The employee was hospitalized with a fractured ankle.

An employee was breaking down a tower crane and removing the boom. His right hand was crushed between the boom as it was being lowered and the crane's turntable. The employee sustained a crushing injury to their hand and the amputation of the index finger.

On May 4, 2025, at approximately 12:45 PM, an employee was walking to her car when she fell and a piece of metal mesh penetrated the skin of her forehead. The employee was hospitalized and required surgery.

An employee was working in a shell buggy and untangling its chain. Untangling the chain caused the buggy to roll and the employee lost his balance, grabbing the shell of the tank to steady himself. The wheel of the buggy then ran over his left thumb, resulting in an amputation.

An employee was outside assembling a 500-ton crane. The employee was connecting the rigging to the boom. He leaned forward to attach the lifting plate on the side of the boom and lost balance while bending over. He fell to the ground approximately 10 feet below, landing on his elbow. The employee was hospitalized with a fractured elbow that required surgery.

Employees were conducting maintenance on the clogged vent pipe of an asphalt distributor truck. The employees went to unclog the tank using a propane torch and a piece of steel rebar. They heated the tip of the rebar with the torch and put it inside the tank. An explosion and a fire occurred. Two employees were injured; one employee was hospitalized with fractured bones and first- and second-degree burns.

On May 5, 2025, an employee was erecting a steel form wall and installing turnbuckles when the top turnbuckle attached to the wall broke and struck them. The employee sustained a laceration to the head.

An employee was setting up to work on a section of roof when he fell approximately 20 feet to the ground. The employee was hospitalized with bleeding that required surgery and a facial fracture that required surgery.
An employee was installing gutters throughout the day when he began feeling nauseous. The employee was hospitalized with dehydration.

An employee was pulling an empty pallet jack through a set of double doors when he lost his balance and fell onto his right hip. He was hospitalized with right hip and femur fractures and required surgery.

An employee was installing HVAC equipment in a customer's attic when he knelt down on a support beam that had a screw sticking up out of it. The employee sustained a puncture to the knee that began swelling and he was hospitalized.

An employee was in a scissor lift, running conduit for an air conditioning system next to a garage door. The door began to rise and the scissor lift tipped over, causing the employee to fall. The employee suffered fractures to the the right hip, two ribs, and the pelvis.

On May 6, 2025, an employee was installing structural steel decking on a roof in approximately 99 F weather when he began experiencing muscle cramps, fatigue, chills, and a headache. The employee was hospitalized with dehydration and a kidney injury.

An employee was cleaning an interior wall from the fourth rung of a 6-foot ladder when they fell to the floor. The employee was hospitalized with fractures to their left wrist, two ribs (third and fourth ribs on the left side), and a punctured lung.
An employee was loading a truck and guiding steel beams onto the truck when his glove became caught between two beams. The employee sustained the amputation of his right middle fingertip.
An employee was jump-starting a skid steer tractor when he stepped back off the trailer and fell, striking the tongue of the trailer. The employee sustained six fractured ribs.

An employee was working the switchboard for a train to move through the plant. He gave the all clear signal, and the train began reversing on the tracks. The employee went to get onto the train as it was moving toward him when he missed the railing and fell underneath the train. The last railcar ran over both of his legs, amputating the legs above the knees.

An employee was on a scaffold setting concrete forms at a construction site. The employee was hoisting up a scaffold stringer and set it down when it slipped. He went to catch it and his finger became caught between the stringer and the scaffold gate. The employee sustained a partial tissue amputation to the right little finger below the last digit and required stitches to his ring finger.
An employee was installing siding from a scaffold approximately three tiers high. The employee fell from the scaffolding to the ground and required surgery for a neck injury.
An employee was reeving the boom cable on a tower crane when his hand was caught between the pulleys and the boom cable, resulting in amputation of four fingers.

On May 7, 2025, at 2:52 PM, an employee was walking on the catwalk (approximately 14" wide grating) in front of the cab of a lattice boom crawler crane. As he was crossing over to climb down from the crane, he missed the grabrail and lost balance. He began falling and did not want to hit the track so he pushed his feet backward, to land on unobstructed ground. The employee was hospitalized with a fracture to his L4 vertebra.
An employee was water jetting a tube bundle when the water stream contacted his right leg, lacerating it above the knee. The employee was hospitalized and the laceration required surgery.

On May 9, 2025, an employee was reattaching a box to the exterior of a pump panel. As he used an impact driver to fasten a screw in the panel's frame, the screw nicked a feeder wire behind the panel, resulting in an arc flash. The employee suffered burns to the right hand and forearm, as well as burns to the fingers of their left hand.
An employee was hit by a piece of 2 x 4 lumber and was found on the floor, bleeding from the head. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was installing safety railings on a rolling single-stage scaffold when the scaffold rolled off the sidewalk. The scaffold collapsed into a yard area and the employee jumped from it as it fell. The employee landed on the sidewalk and sustained a fractured right leg.

An employee was using hand tools to level the base of a parking lot light pole when the LED area light fixture broke off the bracket and struck the employee's head. The employee was hospitalized with a head injury.

An employee was reconfiguring a scaffold after moving it. The employee screwed walk boards together and went to test it when the screws came out and the boards gave way. He fell 16 feet to the ground. The employee was hospitalized with fractures to his T11 and T12 vertebrae.
An employee was operating a rebar bending machine. His left middle finger was caught between the bending pin and the material. He was hospitalized and the finger was medically amputated.
An employee was standing on a concrete wall, stripping concrete forms using a pry bar. The employee fell from the wall to the ground 9 feet below, suffering a fractured back and arm.

An employee was standing on a ladder, using a chipping hammer to remove a concrete masonry unit block wall from around ductwork. Below the block he was removing, a steel lintel above a door became loose. As he was steadying the lintel, a concrete block fell onto his left middle finger. The fingertip was amputated.
An employee was installing a shear wall when it struck their foot, lacerating it. The employee was hospitalized, requiring surgery.
An employee was operating a pull cord for a batch machine when they lost balance and fell to the ground. The employee sustained fractures to their tibia and fibula.

An employee was pulling a hose into a house to spray insulating material. As the employee leaned on a handrail, it gave way and the employee fell from the second floor to the first floor. The employee suffered four broken ribs.
An employee was adding low-voltage current transformers to a photovoltaic system. An arc flash burned the employee.

An employee was climbing onto a dozer to back it off a low boy. He slipped, landed on his feet on the low boy deck, and suffered a broken right tibia and fibula. He was hospitalized, requiring surgery.

At about 9:45 a.m. on May 8, 2025, an employee was standing on an aluminum plank to tape ceiling drywall in a stairwell leading to a second-floor loft in a garage. The plank collapsed, he fell to the steps below, and then tumbled to the bottom of the steps. He suffered cuts and a fracture to his right leg and was hospitalized.

An excavator was hoisting a 4,400-pound trench ditch box, suspended from its hook by manhole chains on a trackhoe bucket. The chains slipped and the ditch box fell onto an employee, causing him to fall to the ground. He was then trapped under the spreaders of the ditch box. He suffered a broken right leg and was hospitalized.

An employee was working from the second level of a scaffold. He fell off the walkway within the first working platform of the scaffold as he was egressing to the ground level. The employee suffered a concussion and was hospitalized.
An employee was loading an excavator onto a trailer. He jumped off the excavator and suffered a spine fracture. He was hospitalized.

An employee was using a fixed ladder to access a gas meter located on the roof of a customer facility. While climbing, the ladder partially detached after an anchor came loose, causing the ladder to shift and pinch the employee's left hand against the building. The employee was hospitalized with an open tuft fracture and subsequent partial amputation to the distal ring finger.

An employee was on a scissor lift, removing pipe from an old sprinkler system using a portable band saw. While he was cutting a section of piping that was supported by a hanger in the ceiling, the hanger gave out. The pipe fell and bounced off the scissor lift; as the employee went to grab it, the saw partially amputated his right index finger and lacerated his right middle finger.

An employee was cutting boards near the edge of the first floor of an apartment building that had lost its roof, and many of its walls, to a fire. He stepped onto a ladder and it toppled over the side of the building and he fell with the ladder. He suffered fractures to a lower-back vertebra and both heels.

A maintenance employee was working on a barge in open water, replacing the belt on a deck winch. After replacing the belt and testing it, the employee was taking a picture of the model number on the belt when the machine started. His hand was pulled into the belt and pulley, resulting in a partial amputation to his index finger.
An employee was standing on top of a flatbed semi trailer, preparing to load a roof curb piece. The employee fell off the side to the asphalt ground, suffering broken ribs and a punctured lung.
An employee was checking the voltage in the disconnect from a transformer. The employee was shocked, suffering electrical burns to extremities.

An employee was moving a light plant. When he pushed on it, its dolly/jack broke. The front of the frame fell, caught his glove, and pulled his hand down with it. It landed on the asphalt, pinching his right ring finger and partially amputating the fingertip.

An employee was on the ground assisting as a mini loader used a fork attachment to load a truck with a 4-foot by 4-foot material box. The load began to slide off the fork and then fell onto the employee. The employee was hospitalized with fractures to his skull, the side of his face, ribs, pelvis, and neck.
An employee was inspecting and measuring the roof of a home. The employee slid off the porch roof and suffered a broken right ankle.

At 9:58 a.m. on May 12, 2025, an employee was cleaning and preparing to caulk concrete joints when a site vehicle, moving forward from park, struck them and dragged them about 20 feet. The employee suffered fractures to their arm, leg, and a rib and was hospitalized.

A skid steer was being used to set fence posts when its bucket fell off and struck an employee who was helping bring fencing material and lay out the posts to be set. He suffered broken ribs on the right side, a broken right hip, and a laceration to the liver, as well as potential fractures to two vertebrae.
An employee was cleaning out and organizing the loft in a barn when they fell to the concrete floor about 10 feet below. He suffered a dislocated hip and a head injury.
An employee was using an acetylene torch to cut piping. A flash fire occurred and burned the employee's left hand, chest, face, and left ear. The employee was hospitalized.

On May 13, 2025, an employee was preparing to install an HVAC system on a roof. The employee detached a retractable lanyard from its anchor point, stepped backward, and then fell through a skylight. They fell about 8 feet, struck a temporary wall, and then fell another 7 feet to the concrete floor below. The employee was hospitalized with a broken shoulder blade, broken ribs, a collapsed lung, and a dislocated finger.
An employee was doing demolition work at a commercial construction site. The employee fell from a roof to a floor, suffered a head injury, and was hospitalized.
An employee was starting a large ventilation blower. Fire/gasoline shot out of the blower and burned his left shoulder and underarm.

An employee was helping with directional bore operations. The drill hit a high-pressure gas line. The employee was thrown up into the air and fell to the ground. The employee suffered injuries to the front and back of the head, a broken wrist, and abrasions to the legs.

An employee was helping reeve a luff cable for a luffing jib crane demobilization. He was guiding cable into the luffer sheaves when his glove caught on a greased portion of the cable. His left hand was pulled into a pinch point between the cable and a spreader bar. He suffered lacerations, a fracture, and a tendon injury to the hand.

An employee climbed a pole approximately 22 feet above ground to install a fiber telecommunications cable. The pole broke approximately 1 foot below ground level while the employee was attached to it, resulting in him falling to the ground and landing on the pole. The employee suffered a fractured tibia.
An employee was lowering a ladder from a first-level roof to the ground so he could climb down it. He lost his balance and fell 12 feet, landing on the ladder and suffering a broken spine.

An employee and their team were fixing a floor tile in the meat department of a supermarket. The employee went to move a large meat grinder when he was electrocuted due to a loose 220-volt ground wire. The employee was hospitalized with an electrical shock to the right shoulder that spread throughout his body.

On May 14, 2025, an employee was on a scaffold measuring and planning where to drill holes. The scaffold collapsed, and the employee fell 8 feet to the ground impacting a nearby metal object. The employee was hospitalized with a back injury that required surgery.

An employee was helping to set concrete traffic barriers by guiding a barrier clamp weighing approximately 600 pounds that was connected to an excavator. The employee guided the clamp down on top of the barrier successfully, which then disengaged the locking pin and allowed the clamp to scissor and grab the barrier to raise it again. As the excavator operator hoisted the barrier clamp to move the segment of barrier, the employee's left ring fingertip got caught in the scissor area of the barrier clamp, resulting in a transphalangeal fingertip amputation.

An employee climbed a pole and was removing fiberoptic line from that pole and placing it on another pole. The pole the employee was climbing twisted and fell along with the employee. Their left leg struck a large rock, resulting in a fractured femur.
An employee was raking gravel in a road lane. A pilot car struck the employee, who suffered fractures to their ribs, tailbone, and right hip.
An employee was setting a water pump to dewater in a small trench when a piece of clay broke off and struck him in the side. The employee sustained a hip dislocation.

An employee was crouched down to remove dirt/debris from around a grader so that it could mark the appropriate grade level. The grader turned left and the right tire struck the employee. The employee was hospitalized with a fracture to the right side of their pelvis and required surgery.

An employee was pushing a steel member on a floor cart when their right index finger was pinched between the steel member and the top supporting edge of the cart. Flesh on the underside of the finger was amputated from the distal phalange.

An employee was helping guide a pipe onto a trailer. A piece of pipe fell off the forks of a loader and the end of the pipe hit the employee's lower right leg. The employee sustained a fracture below their knee.

On May 15, 2025, two employees were laying out waterproofing membrane material on the balcony of a new residence. The injured employee was unrolling the membrane when he stepped off the edge of the roof adjacent to the balcony. The employee fell approximately 13.5 feet to the ground and sustained a fractured pelvic bone.

On May 15, 2025, two employees placed a piece of electrical switchgear inside a modular data center. An employee was using a pry bar to lift the switchgear while the injured employee was removing skates from under the switchgear. The switchgear came down and pinched the injured employee's left index finger. The fingertip and part of the nail were amputated without bone loss.

An employee was unloading a dump bin when something became stuck in the wheel. The employee went to dislodge the object when the bin rolled back and caught his right middle finger between the bin and the wheel. The employee sustained a partial amputation of the finger.
An employee was working on a pole light in front of a hospital when he sustained an electric shock and was hospitalized.

An employee was adjusting a garage door while standing on a 6-foot A-frame ladder when he lost balance and fell from the ladder to the ground below, resulting in three fractured vertebrae in the lower back that required hospitalization and surgery.

An employee descended the stairwell of the flatbed of a traffic control truck and shut the stairwell/platform door behind him. The door shut on his left third finger, resulting in amputation of the fingertip.
On May 16, 2025, an employee crossed over a stand to support a wide flange beam they were fabricating. The beam rolled over onto their lower right leg and foot, resulting in fractures.
